title: Review round 1: kith-jmap JMAP protocol layer
notes:
Maintainer risk review of kith-jmap/src/lib.rs complete.

FINDINGS:

P1 RISKS (2 findings):

1. METHOD_ROLES / register() mismatch (KITH-5r8.1)
   - register() and METHOD_ROLES are decoupled
   - Missing METHOD_ROLES entry causes silent handler death (unknownMethod error)
   - No compile-time or test-time detection
   - Scales poorly as method count grows

2. resolve_args() partial mutation on error (KITH-5r8.2)
   - In-place mutation can leave args in corrupted state if resolution fails
   - Fragile pattern that invites future bugs
   - Not a correctness issue, but hard to debug

LOWER PRIORITY (noted but not filed as issues):
- HandlerFuture boilerplate (ergonomics, not a risk)
- Single file growth (architectural smell, not yet urgent at 1224 lines)

AREAS WITH NO ISSUES FOUND:
- Request parsing (parse_request): solid validation logic with good error messages
- Session object building (build_session): clean implementation with proper fallbacks
- Dispatcher dispatch logic: correct role checking (defense-in-depth at lines 335+)
- Error handling and HTTP status mapping: comprehensive and RFC-aligned
- Test suite: extensive, oracle-based, no self-certifying patterns
- RFC compliance: Request parsing, session objects, error types all correct per RFC 8620

VERDICT: kith-jmap is maintainable at current size. The two P1 risks are addressable without major refactoring. No blocker issues found.
